items.title: Letter 1 — On the One Thing Needful
items.attribution_note: Translated for this edition from the Russian of St Tikhon of Zadonsk (public domain), from the collection he himself compiled under the title Letters Sent — 46 letters of counsel written from his retirement at Zadonsk, 1769–1780, to friends, pastors and people who wrote to him for advice. No English translation of this collection has been published; this is, as far as could be verified, the first. The Russian text the translation was made from is kept in the repository.

items.title: Letter 2 — On the Certain Truth of God's Word
items.attribution_note: Letter 2 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance. This letter and the three following it (Letters 3–5) were originally written by St Tikhon as one continuous treatise, On Faith, which he later divided into four letters for this collection; each is translated here as its own complete letter.

items.title: Word 1 — On Self-Examination
items.attribution_note: Translated for this edition from the Russian of St Tikhon of Zadonsk (public domain), from the cycle he preached and later published as Краткие нравоучительные слова ("Short Moral-Instructive Words"), St Petersburg, 1784 — 27 sermons ("Слово первое" through "Слово двадцать седьмое") plus a 28th appended piece, "О муке вечной и о жизни вечной" (On Eternal Torment and Eternal Life). Source text: azbyka.ru (https://azbyka.ru/otechnik/Tihon_Zadonskij/kratkie-nravouchitelnye-slova/). No prior public-domain English translation of this collection could be found (confirmed via research 2026-08-15); this is, as far as could be verified, the first. The Russian text the translation was made from is kept in the repository.

items.title: The Life and Martyrdom of St Kosmas of Aitolia
items.collection: The Life of St Kosmas of Aitolia
items.attribution_note: Translated for this edition from the Greek of St Nikodemos the Hagiorite's Life and Martyrdom of St Kosmas, written for his New Martyrologion (first edition Venice 1799; Nikodemos died in 1809, so the text is public domain), as reprinted at 24 August in The Great Synaxaristes of the Orthodox Church, whose editors state that they took it from the New Martyrologion and corrected only its phrasing. The eleven notes on places and names at the end are those modern editors', not Nikodemos's, and are translated with credit. Kosmas was hanged in 1779 near Berat in what is now Albania. A WARNING ABOUT ONE SECTION: the section headed 'Jews of Ioannina accuse him of being sent by the Russians' carries language about Jews that is hostile and, in two places, openly hateful — it calls them a 'Christ-hating race' and 'God-killers', and it credits them with plotting the saint's death. That is what the Greek of 1799 says, and it is left here as it stands rather than quietly softened, because a translation that tidies its source is not a translation. It is set down as a record of how the text reads, not as anything the Church teaches or this library endorses. The deicide charge it repeats has been explicitly repudiated in modern Christian teaching. Read that section knowing this.
